title: Temple Grandin
about: the life of Temple Grandin: when and where they were born, their best-known work, discovery or invention and when, a few moments from their life such as moving, studying or a turning point, and when they died if they have. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: Temple Grandin was born on August 29, 1947, in Boston, Massachusetts. She did not speak until she was nearly four years old, and doctors DIAGNOSED her with brain damage. Later she was understood to be autistic. Her mother, Eustacia, refused to send her away and found teachers to help her learn to talk. At a boarding school in New Hampshire, a science teacher named William Carlock became her MENTOR. One summer she visited her aunt's cattle ranch in Arizona, a wide desert land of dust, cactus and cowboys, and she spent hours watching the animals closely.

On the ranch, Temple saw a squeeze chute that calmed nervous cattle. At about 18, she built her own squeeze machine to calm herself. She earned a doctorate in animal science in 1989 and has taught at Colorado State University since 1990. Her most famous work is designing calmer, more HUMANE ways to handle LIVESTOCK, with curved walkways that match how cattle see the world. Nearly half the cattle in the United States and Canada are handled in places she designed. Her books, such as Thinking in Pictures from 1995, and a 2010 film about her life have inspired millions of people. She is still living and still teaching.
